claims.statement: All 186 held orders are in scope EXC-0921 (split reservation created by v18); all orders in EXC-0921 are held; no other orders are held. This establishes v18 rule change as causally linked to the hold state.
claims.limitation: Cannot yet distinguish whether v18 logic is defective or whether east-node lanes handle split reservations differently. Only rule-affected orders routed to east node.

claims.statement: Hypothesis: Allocation rule set v18 contains a defect in split-reservation logic that causes orders to be marked held and not advanced to carrier pickup scheduling.
claims.limitation: Requires confirmation: carrier ops may or may not have received pickup orders; state machine may be blocked downstream.

next_action.rationale: Determine whether Carrier Operations received the 186 EXC-0921 orders and booked pickups for them. If received and scheduled: root cause is in our state machine between allocation and scheduling. If not received: root cause is in our carrier feed/integration. If received but rejected: order data issue (e.g., split reservation format unrecognizable). This diagnostic directly tests the boundary between Inventory Control (allocation) and Carrier Operations (scheduling).
